chapter: Buddy Petit's switch, death and family
title: Foster's parents and their deaths in Mandeville
summary: Foster says relatives remain in Mandeville and tells how his father, a minister, took over a church, brought it out of debt, and died in December.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Any of your folks over there yet?

Yeah. Any of your relatives? Yeah, I have relatives over there yet. I have relatives coming from my wife to see me. I have relatives coming from there last night. In fact, my mother died over there. My father. Did your father die over there, too? My father and my mother died in the middle of the house.
Both died in the middle of the house.
Of course, the house is down on. How long ago did your father die? My father died December 29th. My mother died the last day of February, February 24th.
Your father had the church there all that time?

The church is still there, but there was a tear down there about a month ago. I don't know. The church is still there. The church that he was paying for. The church that he bought out of debt that a preacher had had. You understand? Yeah. And couldn't pay it out. You know, they built it. Lash had seven men built the church. My father picked it. Taking that church. Was ordained minister. He got ordained. And he taken that church over and brought out of debt. And preached and passed through the church until he died. In 29 December, I was here all about four days before Christmas. Or 29. He died. And he didn't stop.
